label: Open Library verification
summary: Open Library verification is a factual grounding step that requires checking whether a book and its attributed author actually exist on Open Library before writing a library entry. It was introduced as a direct response to a hallucination incident where Claude invented a plausible but false author for a non-existent book. The rule is now non-negotiable and documented in CLAUDE.md.
how_maaike_uses: Maaike uses Open Library verification as a structural safeguard against AI confabulation in her garden's library workflow. The rule was added after a specific failure: Claude attributed a made-up book to a real competitor, which she frames not just as a technical error but as a professional integrity risk. The verification step is meant to be baked into the /new-book skill so the check happens before any entry is written, not as an afterthought.
open_questions: A full audit of all ai-assisted library entries against the original Notion source is still pending.
The entry for 'Bacteria to AI' attributed to N. Katherine Hayles needs verification and may itself be a hallucination.
